Hanging bunch of threads tied at one end

Material used for writing or wrapping

Hue, such as red or blue

answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an action, unlike a tool name such as scissors or knife. Matching the clue's part of speech helps narrow the answer.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.GLUE: Glue bonds surfaces together as it sets. Tape holds them with an adhesive already attached to a strip.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.

answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.

answerNotes.SCISSORS: Scissors use two blades moving past one another. Finger loops help control the opening and closing action.
answerNotes.TAPE: Adhesive tape fastens surfaces with a sticky strip. Magnetic recording tape is a different material sharing the same short name.

answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.PHOTO: Photo is short for photograph. A caption or name label can preserve information that the image alone does not supply.
answerNotes.LETTER: Letter can mean a written message or one alphabet character. An envelope clue points to the message sense.
answerNotes.SHELL: Shell means a hard outer covering. The same everyday word can describe the outside of an egg, nut, or crab.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button fastens through a buttonhole or loop. Some have holes through the face; others attach by a small shank on the back.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.GLUE: Glue bonds surfaces together as it sets. Tape holds them with an adhesive already attached to a strip.
answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
